fixes.explanation: True, baker. "And He will redeem Israel from all iniquity." Look at that word "all." After a song that started in the depths, it ends with the LORD redeeming and no iniquity left out. That's a long way up from the bottom.

I get why you'd pick it, since this is a song, after all. But the writer isn't down there celebrating anything. He cries "Out of the depths I cry to You, O LORD!" and what he asks the LORD to hear is his "…plea for mercy." That's the cry, friend, and it's what the verse says.

Not quite, friend. The writer is in the depths, and nothing in the verse says he's leaning on himself. He says, "…in His word I put my hope." His hope rests on the LORD's word, not on how strong he feels. Honestly, my own strength never did much for my worn-out edges.

Yes, baker. David says, "My heart is not proud, O LORD, my eyes are not haughty." He's telling the LORD where his heart stands, and that's some humble talk. Me, I'd have been tempted to mention the hat.

Not this time, baker. David says the opposite: "I do not aspire to great things or matters too lofty for me." He isn't telling the LORD he goes after the big stuff. He's telling Him he doesn't aspire to it.
Right, baker. David says, "I do not aspire to great things or matters too lofty for me." He's not reaching for things beyond him. And he says it straight to the LORD, which makes it even better.
